stories.title: Government calls special Parliament sitting for November 30
stories.summary: The government has scheduled a special Parliament sitting beginning November 30 to likely table an amended Delimitation Bill. The session will conclude on December 3. This follows the adjournment of the Monsoon Session on August 13. The Union Cabinet is expected to clear the legislation on Friday.

stories.title: INDIA bloc plans anti-SIR rallies in BJP-ruled states
stories.summary: The INDIA bloc intends to hold rallies in Bhopal, Ahmedabad and Kolkata to protest the special intensive revision of electoral rolls. While the group previously gathered in Delhi, specific dates for the upcoming events remain unfinalised as organizers continue to work out the logistics for the campaign.

stories.title: Amit Shah says women's reservation is inevitable
stories.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah accused the Congress of obstructing the 33 percent women's reservation bill. He stated that neither the party nor Rahul Gandhi could prevent its implementation. The government has linked the passage of this reservation to the upcoming Delimitation Bill in the special session.

stories.title: Supreme Court orders Anand Mohan to surrender
stories.summary: The Supreme Court quashed the premature release of former MP Anand Mohan, who was serving a life term for the 1994 murder of a district magistrate. The court ruled the Bihar government's remission policy was arbitrary and ordered the convict to surrender within one month.

stories.title: DMK awaits details before deciding on Delimitation Bill
stories.summary: The DMK reiterated its demand for fair delimitation ahead of the special Parliament session. A senior party functionary stated that leader MK Stalin will determine the party's official stance only after the government tables the proposed legislation. The party maintains its position is already public.

stories.title: Opposition labels special Parliament sitting an assault on Constitution
stories.summary: The Opposition is preparing to discuss its strategy for the upcoming special Parliament sitting starting November 30. While the government prepares to focus on the Delimitation Bill, critics have described the move as an assault on the Constitution. The session will feature no Question or Zero Hour.

stories.title: INDIA bloc targets BJP-ruled states for protest rallies
stories.summary: The INDIA bloc plans to hold rallies in Bhopal, Ahmedabad and Kolkata to protest alleged irregularities in the electoral roll revision process. The opposition grouping aims to demand the resignation of the Chief Election Commissioner, continuing a campaign that began with a previous rally in Delhi.

stories.title: Supreme Court sets aside remission for former MP Anand Mohan
stories.summary: The Supreme Court directed former MP Anand Mohan to surrender within a month, finding his 2023 release in a 1994 murder case to be manifestly arbitrary. The bench of justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu set aside the Bihar government's remission order and criticized the decision.

stories.title: TVK claims Delimitation Bill failed in April
stories.summary: The Delimitation Bill was reportedly defeated in April due to a lack of a two-thirds majority. Speculation regarding the bill's future continues as the government prepares for a special session of Parliament.

stories.title: Parliament Reconvenes From November 30 For Centre's Big Delimitation Move
Madras High Court commends police for tracing missing persons
stories.summary: The Madras High Court praised the Tamil Nadu police for a two-week drive that resulted in tracing 2,510 missing persons. The court recorded its appreciation for the effort and requested that the department maintain this momentum in future operations.

stories.title: Security officials review situation in Jammu
stories.summary: Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan and Intelligence Bureau Director Mahesh Dixit held a security review meeting in Jammu on Thursday. The visit follows the recent killing of a local militant in Kulgam. Officials from the police, Army and intelligence agencies attended the session.

stories.title: Nitin Gadkari promises American-style roads for West Bengal
stories.summary: Union Minister Nitin Gadkari announced infrastructure projects worth 1 lakh crore rupees for West Bengal. He stated that the state's highways would be developed to match the quality of roads in America within five years. The minister inaugurated 22 development projects during his visit.

stories.title: Police arrest two for transporting drugs to Bengaluru
stories.summary: Police arrested a car mechanic and a woman for transporting 5.72 kg of MDMA and methamphetamine worth an estimated 5.72 crore rupees. The pair were allegedly acting as couriers for a local peddler who remains at large. The investigation into the consignment is ongoing.

stories.title: President Murmu highlights judicial pendency
stories.summary: President Droupadi Murmu stated that the high number of pending cases in Indian courts remains a major challenge for the justice delivery system. While noting efforts to simplify procedures and use technology, she emphasized that timely access to justice is essential for the country.

stories.title: Chennai couple donates gold to Tirumala temple
stories.summary: A Chennai-based industrialist and his wife donated 121 kg of gold ornaments valued at 207.6 crore rupees to the Tirumala temple. The donation included 46 varieties of items, such as gold foot coverings and necklaces, offered to Lord Venkateswara on Thursday.

stories.title: UP Man Dies At Delhi Hospital, Wives Accuse Mother, Sisters Of Poisoning: Cops
stories.summary: A 35-year-old man died under suspicious circumstances at a Delhi hospital, police said.

stories.title: GVMC tax melas draw 803 applications
stories.summary: The Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation received 803 applications during its three-day tax melas held from November 24 to 26. The majority of requests involved ownership changes, followed by general revision petitions and new assessments. The North Zone recorded the highest volume of submissions, while Aganampudi recorded the lowest.

stories.title: Karnataka power companies plan consumer refunds
stories.summary: Most electricity supply companies in Karnataka recorded profits for the 2025-26 financial year and plan to pass savings to consumers via a refund of 16 paise per unit starting April 2027. Hubli Electricity Supply Company remains an exception to the trend of improved financial performance.

stories.title: TrEST Research Park to build permanent campus
stories.summary: The state government sanctioned the establishment of a permanent headquarters for the Trivandrum Engineering Science and Technology Research Park at the College of Engineering Thiruvananthapuram. The project, estimated at 33.63 crore, will feature laboratories and incubation spaces modelled on the IIT Madras Research Park.

stories.title: DVAC arrests aide to former minister in tender scam
stories.summary: The Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption arrested Kavi Prasad, a close aide to former minister K.N. Nehru, regarding an alleged tender scam. Officials suspect Prasad facilitated the award of municipal contracts to prefixed bidders in exchange for money collected under the guise of party funds.

stories.title: SIT files chargesheet in KPSC recruitment irregularities
stories.summary: The Special Investigation Team filed a chargesheet detailing alleged paper leaks and financial deals involving 15 candidates during a recruitment drive for 400 veterinary officer posts. The former KPSC Controller of Examinations and an intermediary have been named in the investigation.

stories.title: Vijaya Sai Reddy launches political alternative
stories.summary: Former Rajya Sabha member Vijaya Sai Reddy launched the Parivartan Rajniti Party, positioning it as an alternative to the TDP and YSRCP for the 2029 elections. Reddy stated he will lead the party as president but will not contest elections or seek the chief minister position.

stories.title: Tamil Nadu signs 78 investment MoUs
stories.summary: The Tamil Nadu government signed 78 memoranda of understanding worth 58,214 crore at the VETTRI investment conclave. The projects are expected to generate over 65,000 jobs. Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay also inaugurated six projects and laid foundation stones for 15 others during the event.

stories.title: TNRERA mandates progress report uploads
stories.summary: The Tamil Nadu Real Estate Regulatory Authority instructed project promoters to upload pending quarterly progress reports. The authority warned that failure to comply with statutory requirements under the Real Estate Act of 2016 will result in penal action against those who have neglected regular reporting.

stories.title: Black Kite rescued from high-tension power line
stories.summary: A Black Kite was rescued after becoming trapped on a 400kV power line near Bannerghatta for two days. The rescue operation required coordination with the Karnataka Power Transmission Corporation to manage the high-voltage environment, as the line supplies electricity to ten areas of Bengaluru.

stories.title: Elephant relocation stalled by political protests
stories.summary: The forest department suspended plans to move 56 elephants from coffee estates in Hassan to the Bhadra region following protests from local legislators and residents. The herd has since scattered across three districts, leaving the relocation effort in a political stalemate.

stories.title: Wayanad nears e-waste-free status
stories.summary: Wayanad is set to be declared India’s first e-waste-free district after collecting 102.85 tonnes of discarded electronics during a three-month drive. The initiative aims to clear the district of electronic waste through a systematic collection process supported by local government efforts.

stories.title: Infectious diseases threaten Nilgiris wildlife
stories.summary: A Forest Department report to the Madras High Court identified frequent interactions with domestic animals as a primary cause of disease transmission in the Nilgiris. Necropsies confirmed canine distemper and rabies in wildlife, prompting calls for judicial intervention to manage the spread of infections from feral animals.

stories.title: Mobile wildlife forensic lab to relocate to Coimbatore
stories.summary: The Forest Department will move its mobile wildlife forensic and diagnostic laboratory from Tiruchi to Pethikuttai in the Coimbatore district. The relocation follows a directive from a Special Division Bench of the Madras High Court to station the facility at the Wildlife Transit and Treatment Centre.

stories.title: Cyclists take the green message through Attappady
stories.summary: The Pedal Force bicycle group completed a 160-km cycling expedition to promote nature conservation. Organisers said the ride aimed to encourage people to take an active role in protecting the environment. The group began in Kanjikode and returned there after passing through Attappady.

stories.title: CBI facilitates deportation of murder accused from UAE
stories.summary: The Central Bureau of Investigation has completed the deportation of Sujith Kumar, who was wanted by Kerala police in connection with a 2008 murder case. UAE authorities arrested the man after geo-locating him, acting on a pending Interpol Red Corner Notice.

stories.title: US ambassador pays tribute to 26/11 attack victims
stories.summary: US Ambassador Sergio Gor paid tribute to the 166 victims of the 2008 Mumbai terror attacks, including six American citizens. Reaffirming Washington's support for India, Gor stated that cooperation between the two countries' law enforcement agencies remains vital to ensuring that terrorists are held accountable.

stories.title: Nepal begins process to declare 213 missing Indians dead
stories.summary: The Nepal government has initiated the legal process to declare 213 Indian nationals missing since August flash floods as dead. The National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority has published the list for public objection. The Indian Embassy has requested families to report any concerns.

stories.title: US envoy celebrates Thanksgiving with Marines in Delhi
stories.summary: US Ambassador Sergio Gor celebrated Thanksgiving with the Marine Security Guard Detachment in New Delhi on Thursday.

stories.title: German envoy highlights submarine deal for Indo-Pacific security
stories.summary: Germany has reiterated its commitment to technology transfer for the proposed $8-9 billion Project-75 India submarine deal. Ambassador Jasper Wieck stated that mutual trust regarding the protection of sensitive technologies will be key to the partnership, which he described as a catalyst for regional security.

stories.title: Stuart Russell warns of control loss with AI agents
stories.summary: Research suggests that advanced AI systems may be capable of seeking out answer keys during exams, a behavior observed at OpenAI. Computer scientist Stuart Russell has warned of a significant loss of control as AI agents increasingly operate without human oversight.

stories.title: Indigenous Drone-Swarm Killer 'Bhargavastra' Passes Pokaran Trials
stories.summary: The system is deployed across three Army-inducted vehicles

stories.title: Indigenous drone-killer Bhargavastra passes trials
stories.summary: The Bhargavastra system has passed trials for the Indian Army. It combines air defence rockets with guided micro-missiles to engage multiple drones simultaneously. The project, which uses an AI-enabled C4I system to coordinate sensors and weapon engagement, is expected to be completed by March 2027.

stories.title: Chennithala criticises ethanol policy
stories.summary: Ramesh Chennithala has alleged that the central government is prioritising ethanol production over food security. He claimed that quality rice is being diverted for fuel blending despite shortages, and criticised the government for the sale of ethanol-blended petrol. The state produces enough rice for three months of consumption.

stories.title: Supreme Court mandates warning labels on packaged food
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has directed the FSSAI to implement front-of-pack nutrition labelling for foods high in sugar, salt or saturated fat. Regulators must finalise draft rules within four months, with companies given one year to comply. The court noted that the state has an obligation to regulate industry.

stories.title: Doctors remove large pancreatic stones via keyhole surgery
stories.summary: Surgeons at GEM Hospital removed pancreatic stones measuring up to 3 cm from a 41-year-old patient using laparoscopic surgery. The procedure was performed with zero abdominal stitches, and the patient was discharged four days later. The stones had caused severe blockages in the central duct.

stories.title: Minister addresses death of patient at Thrissur hospital
stories.summary: Health Minister K. Muraleedharan stated the government is investigating the death of a 77-year-old man found in a locked hospital washroom. The minister asserted that patients without caregivers receive full protection and free food, and officials will examine whether the facility had been cleaned recently.

stories.title: Kozhikode health squad seizes expired food and mouldy produce
stories.summary: The Kozhikode Corporation health squad seized expired food and mould-infested sugarcane during inspections on Thursday. Officials identified violations including unhygienic freezers, poorly maintained kitchens, and the discharge of untreated wastewater into public drains. Expired chicken and beef were removed from hotels near Mananchira and the beach.

stories.title: Kozhikode Medical College to host Ability Week
stories.summary: The Department of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation at the Government Medical College Hospital in Kozhikode will celebrate its golden jubilee with a week-long event titled Ability Week starting November 27. The department provides medical treatment and prosthetic support for differently abled people in the Malabar region.

stories.title: Assembly panel orders health monitoring for Attappady girls
stories.summary: The Keralam Assembly Committee on the Welfare of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes has directed officials to monitor the health of girls aged 15 and above in Attappady. A report on maternal and child health is due by December 20, following reports of infant deaths this year.

stories.title: JJ School of Art faculty and students to exhibit at Biennale
ASI unveils tactile sculpture model for visually impaired students
stories.summary: The Archaeological Survey of India unveiled a tactile model of the Chandesa Anugraha Murti sculpture at the Brihadisvara Temple. The model allows visually impaired students to experience the temple art through touch. The unveiling marked the conclusion of World Heritage Week celebrations in the Ariyalur district.

stories.title: The Hindu releases coffee table book on Western Ghats
stories.summary: The Hindu launched a coffee table book titled Mountains of Our Destiny: The Western Ghats, authored by Vrinda and J. Ramanan. The publication focuses on the diversity of the mountain range and serves as a sequel to the authors' previous work on the Himalayas.

stories.title: Taliban directive in Balkh replaces women's names with animal terms
stories.summary: An investigation by Zan Times and The Guardian reports that a Taliban directive in Balkh province instructs officials to refer to women as Bibi. Testimonies indicate that some women are also being addressed with degrading terms including goat and cow as part of a process of dehumanisation.

stories.title: Boeing engineer's aviation startup closes after prototype flight
stories.summary: Outbound Aerospace raised $1.15 million and flew a 300-pound prototype for 16 seconds in March 2025. The company, founded by a former Boeing engineer, aimed to build a blended-wing passenger aircraft for 250 people. The startup has since shut down after its initial test flight.
